finding: Full-SoC synthesis may retain inferred memories without a complete implementation inventory
requirement: No unexplained inferred cells in the implementation baseline
status: BLOCKED (ROM now synthesizable; memory macros still not implemented)
evidence: Inventory complete and reproducible from elaboration: exactly 4 inferred $mem_v2 (boot ROM 16 KiB 2R, TCM 32 KiB 2R1W, SRAM 128 KiB 2R1W, 18 B decode LUT) plus register file (1024 bits) and PLIC priority (64 bits); no FIFOs exist (UART FCR reads 0x01). No macro exists: no .lib/.lef/.gds or blackbox in the tree and no memory compiler has run; ARC-043 is PROPOSED only. The gate's memory-design stage reports each memory as BLOCKED by name and exits 2, and structural_policy.json pins the declared $mem_v2 count so a stale inventory fails. | RUN-0018 (ROM gate-level failure): the RUN-0015 'ROM returns X at gate level' result was an ENVIRONMENT DEFECT, not a ROM defect, and that blocker is now closed. The sky130 cell models shipped in oss-cad-suite/examples/eqy/spm declare D_delayed/CLK_delayed/RESET_B_delayed in their behavioural sequential cells and pass them to the UDP without driving them (the assigns live in an uncompiled timing branch), so every flop reads x for the whole simulation, including while held in async reset. Proven by isolation: a lone dfrtp_1 is x in reset, and with the models repaired in a COPY (240 delayed nets driven, 33 supply declarations) the UNMODIFIED RUN-0015 netlist dumps all 4096 words correctly, md5 28c0ab98 identical to the RTL golden dump. An intermediate hypothesis that memory_map dropped the image (inferred from the netlist having no literal constants) was REFUTED and is retracted: a ROM synthesised to gates encodes its table in wiring (shared 12->4096 decode plus OR planes), not in literals; mutating one data driver changes the dump as expected. A memory-free prototype (unique-case ROM, corrected experiment) also passes with 0 diffs at 16,939 cells / 100,574 um2 cell area vs 98,906 um2 for the original (+1.7%). NO density or PPA claim is made: stat -liberty sums cell area only, and 0.75 um2/bit for 131,072 bits is denser than the sky130 SRAM macro (17.4 um2/bit), so it is an artefact until place-and-route exists. The ROM is therefore functionally viable and the RUN-0015 conclusion about it was wrong; whether a standard-cell ROM is the right 16 KiB implementation (timing, real density, power) remains OPEN. | 2026-11-26: boot ROM no longer only behavioural — scripts/fw_build/gen_rom_rtl.py emits a case-based ROM that tb_boot_rom.v matches word-for-word against the behavioural model (1059 checks each), boots the CPU 7/7 through tb_boot, and maps in Yosys to 32,840 $_MUX_ + gates with no $mem cell. That is a mux-tree ROM (large area), not a characterised array, and the TCM/SRAM macros are still PDK-only, so ASIC memory readiness stays BLOCKED.
next_action: ROM: replace the mux-tree decode with a characterised array if area matters. TCM/SRAM: supply the PDK macro models and run a mapped netlist into P&R; the structural policy keeps the gap visible.

finding: I2C standard-mode timing not met: SCL high phase 1 of 4 quarters, START hold and bus-free time too short
requirement: Standard mode 100 kHz: tHIGH >= 4.0 us, tLOW >= 4.7 us, tHD;STA >= 4.0 us, tSU;STO >= 4.0 us, tBUF >= 4.7 us (NXP UM10204 Table 10)
evidence: Measured at the pins with a 300 ns delayed-rise bus model: at pclk 50 MHz / CLKDIV 124 the pre-fix generator gave tHIGH 2.5 us (limit 4.0 us), tHD;STA 2.5 us (limit 4.0 us) and a host-dependent tBUF. RTL now holds SCL high for quarters 1-2, holds SDA for two quarters after START, and spans four quarters in DONE. Re-measured: fSCL 100.00 kHz, tHIGH 4700 ns, tLOW 5300 ns, tSU;DAT 2500 ns, tHD;DAT 20 ns, tHD;STA 5000 ns, tSU;STO 5000 ns, tBUF 14720 ns; 23 checks pass. Controls: a divider far too small fails 8 timing checks; a mutant releasing SCL and SDA together at STOP is rejected as an invalid STOP; a one-quarter START hold fails tHD;STA. 5/5 controls behave as specified.
next_action: Fast mode (400 kHz), clock stretching and repeated START remain unsupported and are documented as such; supporting 400 kHz needs a duty setting this generator does not have.
